proofs.proof_tex:
The exact calculations in \(\texttt{lem:rank-witness-calculations}\) prove legality of both two-node constructions and give, respectively, literal scores \((3,2,2)\), symmetric scores \((3,3,4)\), and symmetric scores \((3,2,3)\).  They also prove legality of the three-node fork and its literal scores \((5,4,5,5)\).  In the first chain and the fork the true baseline is excluded from the literal minimizers; in the first chain the symmetric repair loses uniqueness, and in the second chain it strictly prefers the root intervention.  Thus neither the published score nor its natural symmetric repair supplies the claimed baseline selector.

For each displayed tuple, membership in \(\mathcal M_p\) and \(\texttt{thm:complete-certificate}\) imply that \(\mathsf{Cert}\) accepts and returns the unique true baseline and semantic explanation.  This proves the stated strict replacement on the observed-coordinate fully covered subclass.  Moreover, \(\texttt{prop:squires-rank-failure-full-domain}\) and its normalized-mechanism embedding show that the negative counterexamples, including the open star family, lie in the full domain of Proposition 10.  The positive conclusion remains exactly the one stated here: it is a certificate on \(\mathcal M_p\), not a recovery theorem under general latent mixing.

added_lemmas.statement:
Every member of \(\mathcal M_p\) belongs to the full model class of Squires et al., Appendix F.2, Proposition 10.  Explicitly, take latent dimension \(d=p\), take the paper's mixing matrices to be \(G_{\mathrm{Sq}}=H_{\mathrm{Sq}}=I_p\), and define the normalized mechanism matrices
\[
 \mathcal B_0=\Omega^{-1/2}A,
 \qquad
 \mathcal B_j=\mathcal B_0+e_j
 \bigl(\tau_j^{-1/2}e_j-\mathcal B_0^{\top}e_j\bigr)^{\top}
 \quad(j\in V).
\]
Then \(\mathcal B_j=(\Omega^{(j)})^{-1/2}A^{(j)}\), and the context precision matrices \(\Theta_j=\mathcal B_j^{\top}\mathcal B_j\) satisfy \(\Theta_j=K_j\) for every \(j\in C\).  Thus the embedding preserves every pairwise precision-difference rank and every rank score.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix a member of \(\mathcal M_p\).  Positivity of every entry of \(\omega\) and \(\tau\) makes the diagonal matrices \(\Omega^{-1/2}\) and \((\Omega^{(j)})^{-1/2}\) well defined.  Acyclicity supplies a topological ordering in which \(A=I_p-B\) is triangular with unit diagonal, so \(A\), and hence \(\mathcal B_0=\Omega^{-1/2}A\), is invertible.

For a fixed \(j\in V\), the row-update term in the displayed definition has all rows zero except row \(j\).  Since
\[
 e_j^{\top}\mathcal B_0
   =\bigl(\mathcal B_0^{\top}e_j\bigr)^{\top},
\]
the update replaces row \(j\) of \(\mathcal B_0\) by \(\tau_j^{-1/2}e_j^{\top}\) and leaves every other row unchanged.  On the other hand, \(A^{(j)}\) replaces row \(j\) of \(A\) by \(e_j^{\top}\), while \(\Omega^{(j)}\) replaces its \(j\)-th diagonal entry \(\omega_j\) by \(\tau_j\).  Consequently, row by row,
\[
 \mathcal B_j=(\Omega^{(j)})^{-1/2}A^{(j)}.                  \tag{25}
\]
The matrices in (25) have precisely the single-row normalized-mechanism intervention form used by the full class of Squires et al., with the admissible special choices \(d=p\) and \(G_{\mathrm{Sq}}=H_{\mathrm{Sq}}=I_p\).  Thus this construction is an embedding into that class, not a change of the observable coordinates.

By \(\texttt{def:model-class}\),
\[
 \Sigma_0=A^{-1}\Omega A^{-\top},
 \qquad
 \Sigma_j=(A^{(j)})^{-1}\Omega^{(j)}(A^{(j)})^{-\top}.
\]
Inverting these positive-definite matrices and using (25) gives
\[
 \Theta_0=\mathcal B_0^{\top}\mathcal B_0
 =A^{\top}\Omega^{-1}A
 =\Sigma_0^{-1}=K_0,
\]
and, for every \(j\in V\),
\[
 \Theta_j=\mathcal B_j^{\top}\mathcal B_j
 =(A^{(j)})^{\top}(\Omega^{(j)})^{-1}A^{(j)}
 =\Sigma_j^{-1}=K_j.                                      \tag{26}
\]
Equation (26) implies \(\Theta_c-\Theta_d=K_c-K_d\) for all \(c,d\in C\); taking ranks and then the stipulated sums proves preservation of the rank matrix and all rank scores.

added_lemmas.statement: The two chain specializations in \(\texttt{def:two-node-counterfamilies}\), the fork in \(\texttt{def:three-node-counterfamily}\), and the strict one-root-star region in \(\texttt{def:star-counterfamily}\) are legal members of their respective classes \(\mathcal M_p\).  The first chain has literal scores \((3,2,2)\) and symmetric scores \((3,3,4)\); the second has symmetric scores \((3,2,3)\).  The fork has literal scores \((5,4,5,5)\).  More generally, throughout the star region, the published literal score of the baseline is \(2p-1\), whereas that of the root intervention is \(2p-2\).  The coordinate certificate accepts every one of these tuples and returns its true baseline and semantic explanation.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For the chain \(1\to2\), write \(B_{21}=b\neq0\), \(\omega=(u,v)\), and \(\tau=(t,s)\).  Baseline factorization and the surgery identity give
\[
 K_0=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 u^{-1}+b^2v^{-1}&-bv^{-1}\\
 -bv^{-1}&v^{-1}
 \end{pmatrix},\qquad
 K_1=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 t^{-1}+b^2v^{-1}&-bv^{-1}\\
 -bv^{-1}&v^{-1}
 \end{pmatrix},\qquad
 K_2=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 u^{-1}&0\\0&s^{-1}
 \end{pmatrix}.                                             \tag{27}
\]
All five scalar parameters in both displayed specializations are positive, \(b\neq0\), and the root intervention is effective because \(t\neq u\).  Target \(2\) is nonroot because \(b\neq0\), so its intervention is effective whether or not \(s=v\).  Hence both are in \(\mathcal M_2\) by \(\texttt{def:model-class}\).

At \((b,u,v,t,s)=(2,1,1,3,2)\), (27) becomes
\[
 K_0=\begin{pmatrix}5&-2\\-2&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 K_1=\begin{pmatrix}13/3&-2\\-2&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 K_2=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1/2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Here \(K_0-K_1\) is nonzero diagonal of rank one.  Moreover,
\[
 \det(K_0-K_2)=-2\neq0,
 \qquad
 \det(K_1-K_2)=-7/3\neq0.
\]
Thus
\[
 R=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&2\\1&0&2\\2&2&0\end{pmatrix}.       \tag{28}
\]
The literal convention in Proposition 10 sums columns \(1,2\), giving \((3,2,2)\); summing instead over every component other than the scored component gives \((3,3,4)\).

At \((b,u,v,t,s)=(1,1,1,1/2,2)\),
\[
 K_0=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 K_1=\begin{pmatrix}3&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 K_2=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1/2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The first two pairwise differences have ranks one and two respectively, while \(K_1-K_2\neq0\) and
\[
 \det(K_1-K_2)=2(1/2)-1=0.
\]
It therefore has rank one, so
\[
 R=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&2\\1&0&1\\2&1&0\end{pmatrix},
\]
whose symmetric scores are \((3,2,3)\).

For the fork \(1\to2,1\to3\), all baseline and intervention variances are positive, the root variance changes from \(1\) to \(3\), and each other target is nonroot.  It is therefore legal.  The same factorization gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 K_0&=\begin{pmatrix}14&-2&-3\\-2&1&0\\-3&0&1\end{pmatrix},&
 K_1&=\begin{pmatrix}40/3&-2&-3\\-2&1&0\\-3&0&1\end{pmatrix},\\
 K_2&=\begin{pmatrix}10&0&-3\\0&1/4&0\\-3&0&1\end{pmatrix},&
 K_3&=\begin{pmatrix}5&-2&0\\-2&1&0\\0&0&1/5\end{pmatrix}.
 \end{aligned}                                               \tag{29}
\]
The baseline--root difference has rank one.  The principal \(2\)-by-\(2\) determinants on coordinates \(\{1,2\}\) for \(K_0-K_2\) and \(K_1-K_2\) are \(-1\) and \(-3/2\); those on \(\{1,3\}\) for \(K_0-K_3\) and \(K_1-K_3\) are \(-9/5\) and \(-7/3\).  Each corresponding difference is supported on those two coordinates and hence has rank two.  Finally,
\[
 \det(K_2-K_3)=11/20\neq0,
\]
so that difference has rank three.  Therefore
\[
 R=\begin{pmatrix}
 0&1&2&2\\1&0&2&2\\2&2&0&3\\2&2&3&0
 \end{pmatrix},
\]
and summation over the published columns \(1,2,3\) gives \((5,4,5,5)\).

It remains to verify the claimed open family.  Fix the star of \(\texttt{def:star-counterfamily}\), let
\[
 d=\tau_1^{-1}-\omega_1^{-1}\neq0,
\]
and take a leaf \(j\ge2\).  By \(\texttt{lem:surgery-identity}\),
\[
 K_1-K_0=d e_1e_1^{\top},
 \qquad
 (K_j-K_0)_{\{1,j\},\{1,j\}}
 =\begin{pmatrix}
 -b_j^2/\omega_j&b_j/\omega_j\\
 b_j/\omega_j&\tau_j^{-1}-\omega_j^{-1}
 \end{pmatrix}.                                               \tag{30}
\]
The determinant of the second matrix in (30) is
\[
 -\frac{b_j^2}{\omega_j\tau_j}<0,
\]
so \(\operatorname{rank}(K_j-K_0)=2\).  Subtracting the root difference changes only entry \((1,1)\), and direct expansion yields
\[
 \det\bigl((K_j-K_1)_{\{1,j\},\{1,j\}}\bigr)
 =\frac{d(\tau_j-\omega_j)-b_j^2}{\omega_j\tau_j}\neq0,       \tag{31}
\]
where the last inequality is the strict star condition.  Hence \(\operatorname{rank}(K_j-K_1)=2\).  The region is nonempty: taking every \(\omega_\ell=1\), \(\tau_1=2\), and \(\tau_j=b_j=1\) for all leaves gives \(d=-1/2\) and makes every numerator in (31) equal to \(-1\).  Positivity, \(d\neq0\), \(b_j\neq0\), and the finitely many strict inequalities persist on an open neighborhood.  The changed root variance and the nonzero parent coefficient of each leaf verify effectiveness, so the neighborhood lies in \(\mathcal M_p\).

For every point of this region,
\[
 R_{01}=1,
 \qquad R_{0j}=R_{1j}=2\quad(2\le j\le p).
\]
Thus the published score \(q_c=\sum_{\ell=1}^pR_{c\ell}\) satisfies
\[
 q_0=1+2(p-1)=2p-1,
 \qquad
 q_1=2(p-1)=2p-2.                                           \tag{32}
\]
Finally, every tuple just considered is a member of \(\mathcal M_p\).  Completeness and uniqueness in \(\texttt{thm:complete-certificate}\) therefore imply that \(\mathsf{Cert}\) accepts it and returns its true baseline and semantic explanation.

added_lemmas.statement: The chain, fork, and open star witnesses falsify the observational-context rank-selector conclusion of Squires et al., Appendix F.2, Proposition 10 on its full published model class, not merely on \(\mathcal M_p\): under the normalized-mechanism embedding their context precisions, rank matrices, and scores are unchanged, while the true observational context is not a literal-score minimizer in the first chain, the fork, and the entire star region.  The natural symmetric score also fails, by a tie in the first chain and a strict error in the second.  This is a negative scope transfer only; the positive coordinate certificate is proved on the observed-coordinate fully covered class \(\mathcal M_p\) and does not assert recovery under latent mixing.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By \(\texttt{lem:squires-class-embedding}\), each legal witness in \(\mathcal M_p\) is a point of the full Proposition-10 class, with \(\Theta_c=K_c\) for every context.  Hence no rank or score changes under the embedding.  By \(\texttt{lem:rank-witness-calculations}\), the first chain assigns literal score \(3\) to the observational context and score \(2\) to intervention contexts; the fork assigns the corresponding scores \(5\) and \(4\); and at every point of the nonempty open star region, (32) assigns \(2p-1\) to the observational context and \(2p-2\) to the root-intervention context.  In each case the observational context is not a minimizer, contradicting the asserted conclusion at points inside its published domain.  The same lemma gives symmetric scores \((3,3,4)\) for the first chain, so uniqueness fails, and \((3,2,3)\) for the second, so even minimization fails.

The embedding establishes only inclusion of \(\mathcal M_p\) in the larger published class.  The positive invocation of \(\mathsf{Cert}\) in \(\texttt{lem:rank-witness-calculations}\) instead uses \(\texttt{thm:complete-certificate}\), whose domain is \(\mathcal M_p\).  Therefore the refutation transfers to the full class by restriction, whereas no positive certificate claim is made for models with nonidentity latent mixing.

proposed.statement: Theorem 2 strictly replaces the unknown-baseline promise of Proposition 10 in Squires et al. on the observed-coordinate fully covered perfect-intervention subclass: both two-node constructions are legal members of \(\mathcal M_2\), the first gives literal scores \((3,2,2)\) and symmetric scores \((3,3,4)\), the second gives symmetric scores \((3,2,3)\), and the legal three-node fork gives literal scores \((5,4,5,5)\); in each case the coordinate certificate returns the true baseline and explanation.
proposed.justification: The embedded low-dimensional and open star families locate the failed rank inequality on the full published domain, while the coordinate certificate supplies the valid positive replacement on the observed-coordinate fully covered subclass.
proposed.gap: Proposition 10's unique rank-score minimization fails inside its full published class; neither that negative transfer nor the positive subclass boundary was previously made explicit.
proposed.consumer: Users of the ICML reduction obtain exact regression tests for the failed rank selector and a valid baseline preprocessing certificate when their data satisfy the observed-coordinate fully covered model.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the normalized-mechanism embedding and full-domain rank-failure proposition into the theorem while preserving its current claim and making the negative-scope transfer explicit in its proof spine.

proposed.citation: Gamella, J. L., Taeb, A., Heinze-Deml, C., and Buehlmann, P. (2022). Characterization and Greedy Learning of Gaussian Structural Causal Models under Unknown Interventions. arXiv:2211.14897. Theorem 6 in the 2022 manuscript, renumbered as Theorem 1 in arXiv version 4; Definition 1 and Section 6.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Pin the theorem numbering to the cited version and record the renumbering in arXiv version 4.

proposed.comparator_claim: Appendix F.2 Proposition 10 asserts that the observational context is the unique minimizer of its deviation-rank score on the paper's full causal-disentanglement model class.
Theorem 1 gives sufficiency and worst-case necessity of one intervention per latent node for recovery under the paper's causal-disentanglement setup.
Theorem 4.1 learns mixture parameters efficiently when the number of components is fixed.
Corollary 4.1.1 identifies the interventional Markov equivalence class using mixture samples plus separate observational samples under interventional faithfulness.

Theorem 3.1 is an exact-oracle identification result for finite discrete causal Bayesian networks given \(G\), \(P(V)\), and \(P_{\mathrm{mix}}(V)\): under exclusion and positivity it recovers intervention tuples and their weights, rather than estimating unlabeled component covariances from samples.
Theorems 1 and 3 recover intervention targets and certain parents from designated observational and interventional samples using sparse precision differences under intervention faithfulness.
Theorem 1 proves consistency of UT-IGSP for the interventional Markov equivalence class and unknown targets under interventional faithfulness with segregated regimes.

Theorem 6 in the 2022 manuscript, renumbered as Theorem 1 in arXiv version 4, characterizes \(I\)-equivalence for separately indexed linear-SCM environments with a common coefficient matrix and noise-variance interventions under faithfulness, intervention heterogeneity, and truthfulness; environment labels are retained and perfect row-deletion surgery is not treated.
Theorem 1.1 clusters growing centered nonspherical Gaussian mixtures under near-disjoint total-variation separation with dimension-polynomial cost and weight-dependent factors.
Theorems 4 and 6 give effective-rank operator-norm moment and concentration bounds for sample covariance operators from labeled Gaussian samples.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Record that the rank-selector refutation and rank-only impossibility transfer to the full Proposition-10 class, whereas the coordinate certificate remains a positive result only on the embedded observed-coordinate subclass; also make the Kumar--Sinha and Gamella comparator scopes exact.

prose_updates.tldr: An unordered pooled mixture containing one observational centered Gaussian SEM component and one effective perfect stochastic intervention per labeled node determines its entire semantic explanation without faithfulness. Coordinate-isolated precision pairs identify baseline--root pairs, invariant root marginals orient the baseline, and acyclicity makes row-support target matching unique. These facts yield a sound-and-complete \(O(p^4)\) exact membership certificate on the observed-coordinate fully covered class, plus deterministic discrete recovery under operator error below \(\min\{\lambda/2,\alpha\lambda^2/16,g/8\}\). A normalized-mechanism embedding shows that the legal chain, fork, and open star counterfamilies refute the ICML 2023 rank selector, and indeed every equivariant rank-only selector, on the full published class; this negative transfer does not extend the positive certificate to latent mixing. The end-to-end growing-dimensional component-estimation tail remains an explicit open question.

project_justification.gap: Appendix F.2 Proposition 10 of Squires et al. is the published unknown-baseline rank reduction, but its decisive intervention-versus-intervention rank inequality fails on legal models inside its full domain. Rank compression is more fundamentally insufficient: an embedded open star family defeats every component-permutation-equivariant rank-only selector. Kumar and Sinha's Theorem 3.1 is instead an exact-oracle theorem for finite discrete causal Bayesian networks given \(G\), \(P(V)\), and \(P_{\mathrm{mix}}(V)\), under exclusion and positivity; it is not a sample estimator of unlabeled Gaussian component covariances. Gamella et al. retain separately indexed environments and study noise-variance interventions rather than hidden-baseline perfect row deletion.
project_justification.niche: The observed-coordinate, centered, fully covered perfect-stochastic-intervention subclass has enough entrywise precision geometry for universal identification at every legal parameter point, including unfaithful laws and nonroot interventions that preserve marginal variance. This positive niche is a strict subclass of the Squires et al. latent-mixing domain, although counterexamples inside it transfer negative conclusions to that full domain.
project_justification.fill: The coordinate certificate recovers the baseline, target bijection, weighted DAG, structural and intervention variances, and mixture weights, and it certifies nonmembership in \(O(p^4)\) exact real arithmetic. The normalized-mechanism embedding makes the scope comparison exact: chain, fork, and star witnesses invalidate the published rank selector on its full class, while the entrywise certificate repairs baseline selection only on the observed-coordinate fully covered subclass.

prose_updates.related_work: Squires et al. (2023, Theorem 1 and Proposition 1) introduce the causal-disentanglement setup and precision-difference construction. Their Appendix F.2 Proposition 10 asserts unique rank-score baseline selection on the full published class. The normalized-mechanism embedding proved here places every member of \(\mathcal M_p\) in that class with identical context precisions, so the chain, fork, and star failures refute Proposition 10 on its own domain. The coordinate certificate is a positive repair only for the embedded observed-coordinate fully covered subclass; it does not solve general latent mixing. Appendix G leaves complete membership testing open. Kumar and Sinha (2021, Definition 3.1, Assumptions 3.1 and 3.2, and Theorem 3.1) give an exact-oracle identification result for a finite discrete causal Bayesian network when \(G\), \(P(V)\), and \(P_{\mathrm{mix}}(V)\) are supplied: under exclusion and positivity, their theorem recovers intervention tuples and weights. It neither estimates unlabeled component covariances from samples nor hides the baseline observational law. Kumar, Shiragur, and Uhler (2024, Theorem 4.1) motivate the pooled-mixture front end but fix the number of components; their Corollary 4.1.1 also uses separate observational samples and interventional faithfulness. Varici et al. (2021, Equation (6) and Theorems 1 and 3) give precision-support machinery for a designated observational/interventional pair, with faithfulness-based guarantees, but do not select a hidden baseline. Squires, Wang, and Uhler (2020, Algorithm 1 and Theorem 1) prove UT-IGSP consistency for segregated regimes under interventional faithfulness. Gamella et al. characterize \(I\)-equivalence for separately indexed linear-SCM environments with a common coefficient matrix and noise-variance interventions under faithfulness, intervention heterogeneity, and truthfulness; this is Theorem 6 in the 2022 manuscript and Theorem 1 in arXiv version 4. Their environments remain labeled, and they provide neither an unlabeled-mixture estimation front end nor perfect row-deletion surgery. Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal (2025, Definition 1.5 and Theorem 1.6) study perfect-intervention recovery with a known observational context and non-Gaussian higher-order information. Anderson et al. (2026, Theorem 1.1) and Koltchinskii and Lounici (2017, Theorems 4 and 6) supply techniques relevant to the still-open growing-component mixture-estimation tail.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The population identification, exact membership, and deterministic stability results are confined to the observed-coordinate, centered, fully covered perfect-surgery class \(\mathcal M_p\). The negative comparison is broader: the explicit choice \(d=p\), \(G_{\mathrm{Sq}}=H_{\mathrm{Sq}}=I_p\), and normalized mechanism matrices embeds \(\mathcal M_p\) into the full class of Squires et al. without changing context precisions, so the rank-selector counterexamples and equivariant rank-only impossibility hold on that full class by restriction. No positive recovery or certificate under latent mixing is claimed. The exact certificate can semantically validate and initialize the documented causaldag unknown-target IGSP workflow by supplying baseline and target labels for an accepted population tuple, but it does not create segregated samples, regime metadata, or empirical testers. The growing-dimensional component operator-error tail remains open. The restriction \(p\ge2\) is necessary because at \(p=1\) the two distinct variances admit both baseline orientations. Missing interventions, soft or multitarget interventions, cycles, singular components, and latent coordinate mixing remain outside the positive theorem.

statement_notes.justification: The embedded low-dimensional and open star families locate the failed rank inequality on the full published domain, while the coordinate certificate supplies the valid positive replacement on the observed-coordinate fully covered subclass.
statement_notes.gap: Proposition 10's unique rank-score minimization fails inside its full published class; neither that negative transfer nor the positive subclass boundary was previously made explicit.
statement_notes.consumer: Users of the ICML reduction obtain exact regression tests for the failed rank selector and a valid baseline preprocessing certificate when their data satisfy the observed-coordinate fully covered model.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(p\geq 2\) and a member of the one-root star family in
\(\texttt{def:star-counterfamily}\).  Thus vertex \(1\) is the root, and,
for each \(j\in\{2,\ldots,p\}\), the only edge into \(j\) is
\(1\to j\), with coefficient \(b_j\neq 0\).  Consequently the transposes
of the structural-equation rows are
\[
 a_1=e_1,
 \qquad
 a_j=e_j-b_j e_1\quad (j=2,\ldots,p).
\]
All baseline and intervention variances are strictly positive by the
definition of the family.  Put
\[
 d=\tau_1^{-1}-\omega_1^{-1}.
\]
The root intervention is effective precisely as required here because
\(d\neq 0\).  By \(\texttt{lem:surgery-identity}\),
\[
 \Delta_1=d e_1e_1^{\top}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
For a leaf \(j\geq 2\), the same identity gives
\[
 \Delta_j
 =\tau_j^{-1}e_je_j^{\top}
  -\omega_j^{-1}(e_j-b_je_1)(e_j-b_je_1)^{\top}.                 \tag{2}
\]
Hence \(\Delta_j\) vanishes off the rows and columns indexed by
\(\{1,j\}\), and its principal matrix on those coordinates is
\[
 \left.\Delta_j\right|_{\{1,j\}}
 =
 \begin{pmatrix}
 -b_j^2/\omega_j & b_j/\omega_j\\
 b_j/\omega_j & \tau_j^{-1}-\omega_j^{-1}
 \end{pmatrix}.                                                  \tag{3}
\]
Direct expansion, using \(b_j\neq0\), \(\omega_j>0\), and
\(\tau_j>0\), yields
\[
 \det\!\left(\left.\Delta_j\right|_{\{1,j\}}\right)
 =-\frac{b_j^2}{\omega_j\tau_j}<0.                              \tag{4}
\]
It follows from (4) that
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(K_j-K_0)
 =\operatorname{rank}(\Delta_j)=2.                              \tag{5}
\]
Likewise, subtracting (1) from (3) and expanding gives
\[
 \det\!\left(
   \left.(\Delta_j-\Delta_1)\right|_{\{1,j\}}
 \right)
 =\frac{d(\tau_j-\omega_j)-b_j^2}{\omega_j\tau_j}.              \tag{6}
\]
The strict inequality in \(\texttt{def:star-counterfamily}\) makes the
numerator in (6) negative, so it is nonzero.  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(K_j-K_1)
 =\operatorname{rank}(\Delta_j-\Delta_1)=2.                     \tag{7}
\]
Finally, (1) and \(d\neq0\) imply
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(K_1-K_0)=1.                                \tag{8}
\]

Let \(\sigma\) be the transposition of component vertices \(0\) and
\(1\).  Equations (5) and (7) say that, for every leaf-intervention
vertex \(j\geq2\),
\[
 R_{0j}=R_{1j}=2,
\]
while (8) gives \(R_{01}=R_{10}=1\).  Entries whose two indices are leaf
vertices are unchanged by \(\sigma\), simply because \(\sigma\) fixes
both indices.  The diagonal entries are zero.  These cases exhaust the
entries of \(R\), and hence, with \(P_\sigma\) the permutation matrix of
\(\sigma\),
\[
 P_\sigma R P_\sigma^{\top}=R.                                  \tag{9}
\]

The strict region used above is nonempty and open relative to the
continuous parameter space of this fixed star graph.  Indeed, take
\[
 \omega_k=1\quad(k\in V),\qquad
 \tau_1=2,\qquad
 \tau_j=1\quad(j\geq2),\qquad
 b_j=1\quad(j\geq2).
\]
Then \(d=-1/2\), and for every leaf
\[
 d(\tau_j-\omega_j)-b_j^2=-1<0.
\]
All variances are positive, the root variance changes, and every leaf
has a nonzero parent coefficient.  Thus all interventions are effective,
including the leaf interventions whose intervention variance equals their
baseline noise variance.  Positivity, \(d\neq0\), nonzero coefficients,
and the finitely many displayed strict inequalities persist on a
neighborhood by continuity.  By \(\texttt{def:model-class}\), that
neighborhood lies in \(\mathcal M_p\).

Now let \(F\) be any rank-only baseline selector that is equivariant under
permutations of the component vertices.  By
\(\texttt{def:rank-compression}\), equivariance means
\[
 F(P_\gamma R P_\gamma^{\top})=\gamma(F(R))                     \tag{10}
\]
for every component permutation \(\gamma\).  Applying (10) with
\(\gamma=\sigma\) and using (9) gives
\[
 F(R)=\sigma(F(R)).                                              \tag{11}
\]
Neither \(0\) nor \(1\) is fixed by \(\sigma\).  Thus (11) implies in
particular that \(F(R)\neq0\), although component \(0\) is the
observational baseline.  The selector therefore fails at every point of
the nonempty open family.  Since \(F\) was arbitrary, no
component-permutation-equivariant rank-only selector universally recovers
the baseline on \(\mathcal M_p\).

For completeness, this obstruction is not confined to the
observed-coordinate subclass of the model in Squires et al.~
\cite[Appendix F.2, Proposition 10]{pmlr-v202-squires23a}.  We verify the
required restriction to their full published domain explicitly.  In the
notation of that model, take latent dimension \(d=p\), observation and
mixing matrices \(G_{\mathrm{Sq}}=I_p\) and
\(H_{\mathrm{Sq}}=I_p\), and define the normalized mechanism matrices
\[
 \mathcal B_0=\Omega^{-1/2}A,
 \qquad
 \mathcal B_j
 =\mathcal B_0
  +e_j\bigl(\tau_j^{-1/2}e_j-\mathcal B_0^{\top}e_j\bigr)^{\top}
 \quad(j\in V).                                                  \tag{12}
\]
The matrix \(\Omega^{-1/2}\) in (12) is well defined because \(\Omega\)
is diagonal with strictly positive entries.
The additive term in (12) has only row \(j\) nonzero.  Moreover,
\[
 e_j^{\top}\mathcal B_j
 =e_j^{\top}\mathcal B_0
  +\tau_j^{-1/2}e_j^{\top}-e_j^{\top}\mathcal B_0
 =\tau_j^{-1/2}e_j^{\top},                                      \tag{13}
\]
whereas every other row agrees with \(\mathcal B_0\).  Thus (12) is
exactly the normalized single-row perfect intervention allowed by the
published class.  It is nontrivial: for a nonroot, the baseline row has a
nonzero parent entry, while for a root effectiveness gives
\(\tau_j\neq\omega_j\), so in both cases
\(\mathcal B_j\neq\mathcal B_0\).  A topological ordering makes \(A\)
unit triangular; deleting the off-diagonal entries of one row leaves it
unit triangular.  Consequently \(\mathcal B_0\) and every
\(\mathcal B_j\) are nonsingular, using the strict positivity of all
variances.

Writing the baseline row vectors as above, (12)--(13) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal B_0^{\top}\mathcal B_0
 &=A^{\top}\Omega^{-1}A
  =\Sigma_0^{-1}=K_0,\\
 \mathcal B_j^{\top}\mathcal B_j
 &=\sum_{k\neq j}\omega_k^{-1}a_ka_k^{\top}
   +\tau_j^{-1}e_je_j^{\top}
  =(A^{(j)})^{\top}(\Omega^{(j)})^{-1}A^{(j)}
  =\Sigma_j^{-1}=K_j.                                           \tag{14}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here the inverse equalities follow respectively from
\(\texttt{ass:baseline-gaussian-sem}\) and
\(\texttt{ass:perfect-single-node-surgeries}\), with invertibility just
verified.  Because \(G_{\mathrm{Sq}}=H_{\mathrm{Sq}}=I_p\), the
published precision objects satisfy
\(\Theta_j=\mathcal B_j^{\top}\mathcal B_j=K_j\).  Therefore every
member of \(\mathcal M_p\), and in particular the open star family above,
embeds into the full Proposition-10 class with exactly the same pairwise
rank matrix.  A selector universally correct on that full class would
restrict to a universally correct selector on the embedded star family,
contradicting (11).  Hence no component-permutation-equivariant rank-only
selector universally recovers the observational context on the full
Squires Proposition-10 class.  This transferred negative conclusion does
not assert positive recovery under latent mixing.
